paper_metadata.title: Mechanical properties and high-temperature deformation behaviour of particle-strengthened NiAl alloys

evidence.quote: Alloying of NiAl with Ta or Nb leads to an alloy with high high-temperature strength.

(b) alloy 1 (PM) with fine Laves-phase particles in a NiAl matrix
The cast alloys were produced by directional solidification (DS).
Powder metallurgy (PM) was applied to gas-atomised powders.
Consolidation was done by hot isostatic pressing (HIP) at 1250 °C.
Forging of the alloys was done by thermomechanical treatments (TMT) with constant strain rate at 1100°C.
alloy 1 (cast) with the Laves phase on NiAl phase boundaries (bright)
alloys with volume contents of 8 to 40% Laves phase form a cellular structure of Laves phase separating the NiAl grains
chromium-rich particles are precipitated as small particles in the NiAl phase
these alloys contain a fine Laves-phase distribution within a NiAl matrix
The cellular structure has been destroyed by forging, and particles are spheroidized in the NiAl matrix.
